model: owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10-year, equity-flow basis at AUD cost of equity)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report, consolidated statement of changes in equity: movement in share-based payments reserve A$17.0m (line 5200). The group SBP expense line is not separately disclosed in the FY26 notes; FY25 expense was A$9.7m. SBC is equity-settled via on-market purchase (A$6.0m treasury purchases FY26); no equity-award withholding tax line exists, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc.
inputs.share_count_basis: 195,409,849 ordinary shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 AR five-year summary, line 8464; diluted weighted average 194,617,746). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The DRP (A$56.9m of shares issued FY26, ~1m shares/yr) is dividend reinvestment, not issuance for value -- the cash it retains is inside the modelled FCF, so charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost: FY26 lease cash A$22.5m (principal A$12.8m financing + interest A$9.7m) deducted inside adj. EBITDA; lease liabilities (A$215.2m, mostly the 39 Martin Place head office) EXCLUDED from net debt; tax-shield D&A excludes ROU depreciation (A$20.0m).

net_debt_bridge.note: ASX Group own cash and short-term investments A$1,485.2m (cash 680.8 + financial assets 9,965.9 - amounts owing to participants 9,161.5; note 25.2) less regulatory capital and licence financial-resource requirements A$1,235.0m = A$250.2m available. Regulatory capital is an operating asset the CCP/SSF licences require, so it stays out of the bridge and its interest stays in the flows; only the surplus A$250.2m is credited and its ~A$9.4m interest stripped (matching-asset rule). The FRN (A$275m 3-yr floating rate notes, Feb-2027 maturity, assumed refinanced) is deducted at par and its interest removed from the flows. The A$132.9m ASIC NTA shortfall (minimum NTA A$1,189.7m by 30-Jun-2027 vs A$1,056.8m) must be retained from FY27 earnings and is treated as permanently locked -- if ASIC releases it after Accelerate milestones the model is ~A$0.5/share too low. Consolidated 'cash_and_equivalents' (A$680.8m) is NOT used anywhere: it commingles participant margin investments and its definition changed in FY2019.

fy0_component_build.tie_out_formula: uNPAT 536.4 + D&A 68.2 - capex 189.0 - lease principal 12.8 - reg-capital build 20.0 - surplus interest after tax 6.6 + FRN/borrowing interest after tax 13.2

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, AUD: 10-yr ACGB ~4.4% + 0.85 beta x 5.5% AUD ERP = 9.1%, used 9.0%. Flows are post-interest (NII net of FRN/lease financing is inside adj. EBITDA) so no debt-weighted WACC applies. Same rate in all three scenarios -- governance/regulatory/CHESS risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights (owner-fcf.md 7f), not stacked on the discount rate.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component-built (owner-fcf.md section 2) on a 10-year horizon, on an EQUITY-flow basis discounted at the AUD cost of equity. The dcf-methods routing table has no exchange/FMI row; ASX is an operating company with real, lumpy capex (A$189m vs A$68m D&A), which is why an earnings-at-CoE bank-style model was rejected -- it would capitalise underlying NPAT and hide the A$120m/yr capex-over-D&A gap that the CHESS programme has opened. Participant margin balances (A$9.2bn owing to participants) are neither deposits to be lent nor net debt; they are pass-through collateral, invested by the CCPs, and are excluded entirely.

REPORTED FCF IS UNUSABLE: OCF-capex (A$73.1m FY26, -A$3,507m FY23, +A$4,994m FY21) swings with participant margin flows. last_fcf is therefore the FY26 component build (A$389.9m), tied to the underlying-NPAT bridge (A$389.5m). The identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does not hold; reported_fcf is retained for auditability only.

EARNINGS BASIS: modelled from UNDERLYING (segment) EBITDA of A$765.0m, which still includes the A$30.8m of FY26 ASIC Inquiry costs. The A$59.8m pre-tax significant items (ASIC penalty and costs A$23.5m, CHESS Partnership Program A$23.0m, Sympli loss A$13.3m) are excluded from the FY0 flows as one-offs, but the forward margin path assumes ongoing Accelerate/remediation spend rather than a return to FY25 cost levels.

INTEREST: net interest income (A$73.2m) is split. Net interest on participant collateral (A$46.2m, a 16bp spread on A$11.9bn) is operating CCP income and stays in the flows. Interest on ASX's own funds (A$55.6m gross) is kept for the A$1,235m regulatory-capital portion (operating asset, not in the bridge) and stripped for the A$250m surplus (in the bridge). FRN/borrowing interest (A$18.9m) is removed from the flows because the FRN principal is deducted in the bridge. Lease interest stays in the flows (treatment B).
REVENUE SERIES: segment operating revenue ex interest, consistent across all 22 periods; FY26 A$1,254.6m.

ASIC CAPITAL CHARGE: A$150m additional NTA by 30-Jun-2027 (shortfall A$132.9m at Jun-26) funded by the payout cut to 75% and a discounted DRP. Modelled as a debt-like bridge item, not a flow, because it is a one-off lock-up rather than a recurring cost. Growth-driven regulatory-capital build is modelled as negative working capital (-13.5% of incremental revenue).

WEIGHTS 25/50/25 (house default 15/50/35): bear raised for single-regulator dependency (ASIC/RBA gate both the capital charge and the CHESS timetable), a demonstrated technology-execution failure precedent, and CEO/CFO transition; bull cut because it needs cost discipline, CHESS Release 2 on time AND capital-charge release to coincide.

BAND POSITION: SBC is ~1.2% of revenue so the house/street band is only A$1.4/share wide and the A$56.74 price sits far above the street ceiling (band_position 6.8 = 676%). Read it as 'the market is paying well above either accounting regime', not as an SBC finding.
PRICE: Yahoo regular-session quote 2026-09-21T06:10Z (ASX close, AUD). Not after-hours. refresh_price.py rewrites price-derived fields.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 1.3% vs revenue 5.7% and underlying EPS 2.1%: equity does not compound because ASX pays out 75-90% of NPAT (and paid a A$696m special-year dividend in FY20), so book-value CAGR is not the growth anchor here. Owner-FCF proxy CAGR is -1.0% over both 3 and 5 years: revenue grew 5-7%/yr but cash capex tripled (A$61m FY17 to A$189m FY26) on CHESS, so none of the revenue growth reached owners. The base case assumes that reverses as capex normalises after Release 2 -- that assumption, not revenue growth, is what the valuation rests on.
historical_growth.eps_basis: underlying EPS (statutory FY26 EPS 2.493 is after A$51.5m significant items)
historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner-FCF proxy = underlying NPAT + D&A - cash capex - lease principal (pre regulatory-capital build)
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF CAGR is meaningless (participant flows). The owner-FCF proxy is flat-to-down for five years while revenue compounded at 5.7%, because SBC is trivial (1.2% of revenue) but capex went from 8% to 15% of revenue.

base.ebitda_margin_basis: owner adj. EBITDA, pre-SBC: segment EBITDA + SBC add-back + net interest on participant collateral + interest on regulatory capital - lease principal and interest. FY2026 actual 67.9% (70.4% ex the $30.8m ASIC Inquiry costs).
base.da_pct_basis: D&A EXCLUDING right-of-use depreciation (tax shield only; added back). FY2026 actual 3.8%; ramps as CHESS Release 1/2 capitalised software (A$509.6m at Jun-26) amortises.
base.capex_pct_basis: cash payments for intangibles + PPE / operating revenue. FY2026 actual 15.1% (A$189.0m, of which A$95.2m CHESS). Pre-CHESS FY2017-19 ran 6.5-8.7%.
base.wc_capture_basis: NEGATIVE: regulatory capital build as % of incremental revenue (FSS default + non-default risk capital grows with clearing exposure and opex). Calibrated to FY2026: +A$20.0m on +A$147.4m revenue.
base.narrative: Franchise intact, costs stay elevated. Revenue +5%/yr near term (5-yr CAGR 5.7%), fading to 3% as FY26's record futures/cash-market volumes normalise but listings recover and super-pool growth continues. Owner EBITDA margin 68% in FY27 (FY26 ex-Inquiry 70.4% less continued Accelerate/technology cost growth and lower own-funds rates), recovering to 70% by FY32 once CHESS Release 2 is delivered (late FY28/FY29 assumed). Capex stays at 14-14.5% of revenue through FY28 then falls to a 9% run-rate; D&A rises to 8.5% as capitalised software amortises. Regulatory capital grows with the business; the A$132.9m ASIC NTA charge is treated as permanently locked (conservative).

bull.ebitda_margin_basis: owner adj. EBITDA, pre-SBC: segment EBITDA + SBC add-back + net interest on participant collateral + interest on regulatory capital - lease principal and interest. FY2026 actual 67.9% (70.4% ex the $30.8m ASIC Inquiry costs).
bull.da_pct_basis: D&A EXCLUDING right-of-use depreciation (tax shield only; added back). FY2026 actual 3.8%; ramps as CHESS Release 1/2 capitalised software (A$509.6m at Jun-26) amortises.
bull.capex_pct_basis: cash payments for intangibles + PPE / operating revenue. FY2026 actual 15.1% (A$189.0m, of which A$95.2m CHESS). Pre-CHESS FY2017-19 ran 6.5-8.7%.
bull.wc_capture_basis: NEGATIVE: regulatory capital build as % of incremental revenue (FSS default + non-default risk capital grows with clearing exposure and opex). Calibrated to FY2026: +A$20.0m on +A$147.4m revenue.
bull.narrative: New CEO delivers. Cost discipline arrives with the Attia/Accelerate reset, CHESS Release 2 lands on the revised timetable, ASIC releases the A$150m capital charge from FY28 and the payout returns to 80-90%. Revenue +8% in FY27 on sustained rate-volatility-driven derivatives volumes and a fuller IPO window, fading to 3.5%. Owner EBITDA margin recovers to 72% (FY16-19 segment margins were 70-71%). Capex normalises faster (8% by FY33). Terminal growth 3.5%.

bear.ebitda_margin_basis: owner adj. EBITDA, pre-SBC: segment EBITDA + SBC add-back + net interest on participant collateral + interest on regulatory capital - lease principal and interest. FY2026 actual 67.9% (70.4% ex the $30.8m ASIC Inquiry costs).
bear.da_pct_basis: D&A EXCLUDING right-of-use depreciation (tax shield only; added back). FY2026 actual 3.8%; ramps as CHESS Release 1/2 capitalised software (A$509.6m at Jun-26) amortises.
bear.capex_pct_basis: cash payments for intangibles + PPE / operating revenue. FY2026 actual 15.1% (A$189.0m, of which A$95.2m CHESS). Pre-CHESS FY2017-19 ran 6.5-8.7%.
bear.wc_capture_basis: NEGATIVE: regulatory capital build as % of incremental revenue (FSS default + non-default risk capital grows with clearing exposure and opex). Calibrated to FY2026: +A$20.0m on +A$147.4m revenue.
bear.narrative: Regulatory ratchet. CHESS Release 2 slips again (Drop 5 already moved to Oct-26), remediation and Accelerate spend persist, ASIC's 2025 access/pricing rules and TMX Australia (ex-Cboe, ~20% share) cap trading-fee economics, and FY26's record volumes mean-revert (flat revenue FY27, then 1.5-3%). Owner EBITDA margin compresses to 64-65% and never recovers; capex stays at 15% through FY28 and 10% thereafter. Capital charge not released. Terminal growth 2.5%.

entry_price.method: price at which the scenario's 10 interim owner FCFs plus a year-10 terminal value REBUILT at the 15% hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, 20x FCF10)), less net debt, return 15% IRR; probability-weighted across scenarios

required_return_table.note: each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon, 20x), floored at 0); the 9% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. Today's A$56.74 sits above the 9% row -- the price implies a required return below ~8% on the base flows.

sensitivity.note: rows = cost of equity, columns = terminal growth. Cells at 7% (and 8% with g >= 3%) are 20x-cap-bound, which is why they flatten.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (vs 15% default): ASIC/RBA are a single regulator gating both the A$150m capital charge and CHESS Release 2 sign-off, the 2022 CHESS abandonment is a demonstrated execution-failure precedent, and the CEO and CFO both changed in 2026. Bull 25% (vs 35%): the bull case needs three independent things to coincide -- cost discipline under the new CEO, Release 2 on the revised timetable, and ASIC releasing the capital charge -- and FY26 volumes were a record it must also hold. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ASX is a regulated near-monopoly whose owner cash flow has not grown for five years because the CHESS rebuild absorbed all the revenue growth. The valuation is a bet on capex normalising after Release 2; at A$56.74 the market is paying ~20.6x underlying EPS and a 3.5% owner-FCF yield for that normalisation plus a return to 70%+ margins, which is roughly the bull case.
key_sensitivities: capex run-rate after CHESS Release 2 (each 1pp of revenue in perpetuity is ~A$2.5/share)
owner EBITDA margin trajectory vs the FY16-26 slide from 71% to 61% segment margin
release of the A$150m ASIC capital charge (~A$0.5/share, not modelled)

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is earnings_at_coe: P/E and EV/EBITDA trip rules do not apply; the historical table is reported for context only
